cross-05-bili.coverage: Envoy capture of the video page plus a local ASR transcript with [mm:ss.mmm] timestamps; the recognition quality is poor (e.g. 文太相物, 不顺格, 深度系形的炭), the transcript is 2433 characters and stops before any end-of-video summary, so spoken detail beyond the captured segments is out of scope.

cross-05-wechat.coverage: Envoy page-level capture of the article body and headings (5298 characters); inline figures with △ markers were not read, so claims that live only in the diagrams are out of scope.

deliverable: A source-grounded comparison of what a multimodal project produces on screen in one Bilibili demo and what a WeChat article says must be produced before an image score can be trusted, citing ASR timestamps and article headings and stating plainly where the two never meet.

turns.text: Using only these two snapshots, describe what each source says a vision model puts out. For the Bilibili video cite the [mm:ss] timestamp of each claim and quote the transcript exactly, including its recognition errors; for the WeChat article cite the heading. Then say which of the two discusses judging the output and which does not, and do not credit either source with a claim it never makes.

Take the Bilibili demo's generation step and the WeChat article's evidence pipeline in turn. For the video, explain from the transcript what modality the script is asked to emit at [03:37.020] and what the presenter points at after the run at [04:16.560], keeping the garbled terms verbatim. For the article, name the 7 perception attributes and the number of visual-evidence tools, and give the reported average PLCC/SRCC, each under its heading.

Now state the gaps explicitly. Does the captured Bilibili transcript ever mention scoring, a metric, a benchmark or a quality judgement? Does the WeChat article describe running a demo, a dataset of depth or detection outputs, or a video? Name any claim in one source with no counterpart in the other, note that the video transcript is ASR text whose garbled terms must not be silently corrected, and cite a timestamp or heading for every point you do assert.

reference_facts.claim: The video opens by announcing the current state of the presenter's multimodal project, which the ASR renders as 文太相物 (a recognition error for a multimodal term that the transcript never spells correctly); the intended object is a multimodal model, not a text-only one.
reference_facts.quote: 我们的文太相物现在的最新发展

reference_facts.claim: While walking through the generation script, the presenter says the output is switched from infrared to visible light plus a depth-style channel; the ASR writes the modality words as 火外魔炭, 可見光 and 深度系形的炭, so the passage shows a multimodal output being produced but not what the model emits downstream.
reference_facts.quote: 我現在打成可見光跟深度系形的炭

reference_facts.claim: After running the demo the presenter says the model has been 端确把握了 (ASR garble) and points to 多么太特有的一些性情, i.e. multimodal-specific behaviour he considers visible in the output; the transcript never states a quality score, a metric or a judging criterion.
reference_facts.quote: 可以看到我们的模型已经被端确把握了,大家可以看到它有一些多么太特有的一些性情

reference_facts.claim: The article's root-cause claim is that current MLLM scoring relies on semantic-biased internal visual representations rather than verifiable low-level degradation evidence, so the model has no information with which to perceive noise or blur and can only guess.
reference_facts.locator: 大模型打质量分，为什么会“凭感觉”？
reference_facts.quote: 现有MLLM打分，依赖的是带有语义偏见的内部视觉表征，而不是可验证的底层退化证据。

reference_facts.claim: To supply that missing evidence the team defined 7 key perception attributes (structure, sharpness, noise, artifact, brightness, colour, naturalness) and built 15 visual-evidence tools from them, each of which renders one degradation into a structured evidence image.
reference_facts.locator: 核心思路：给大模型配一个“检测工具箱”
reference_facts.quote: 团队梳理出IQA中7个关键感知属性——结构、锐度、噪声、伪影、亮度、色彩、自然度，并据此设计了15种视觉证据。

reference_facts.claim: The reported result is a composite SOTA over 7 image-quality benchmarks with average PLCC/SRCC of 0.795/0.784, which the article presents together with an interpretable, traceable evaluation process rather than a bare score.
reference_facts.quote: IQA-T1取得了综合最优（SOTA）的成绩，平均PLCC/SRCC达到0.795/0.784

acceptable_partial_outcomes: The Bilibili transcript is local ASR with heavy recognition errors and stops mid-flow; answers must quote it as-is, may gloss a garbled term only when they flag it as a guess, and must not invent a timestamp.
The captured transcript never mentions scoring, metrics or benchmark numbers, so an answer that says the video evaluates image quality is wrong.
The WeChat article's figures marked with △ were not read; no answer may claim to have inspected them.

reference_review.method: every quote re-checked as a literal substring of the stored snapshot after squashing whitespace

authority_anchors.supports: independent record of teaching LMMs to produce visual quality scores (Q-Align), used to check that scoring an image with a multimodal model and reporting it as a correlation against human opinion is a separately documented task rather than something the WeChat article invented
